title: Policy compiler for hybrid-target autoscaling with staged safety limits
creator: Rohan Patel
description:
Goal: Build a policy compiler that transforms high-level autoscaling policies (user intent expressed in the Console or API) into an executable scaling plan for Dedicated pools. The compiler must support hybrid target specifications (mixes of req/s, tokens/s, p99 latency, queue depth, and GPU util), multiple scaling algorithms (threshold, PID, rate-based smoothing, and a lightweight predictive option), and enforce staged safety limits (pre-scale checks, in-flight caps, and post-scale stabilization invariants).

Scope:
- Design a compact policy DSL and JSON schema that Console/SDK can submit.
- Implement a compiler module that resolves policies to per-pool runtime configs (per-variant knobs: target metric weights, algorithm selection, step limits, cooldown windows).
- Integrate safety checks: global/min/max replicas, max_scale_delta_per_minute, cooldowns, emergency circuit-breaker when observed error-rate or tail-latency spikes.
- Add telemetry hooks and rollout knobs for canaries (percent of traffic) and progressive relaxation.

Why this differs: Existing work focuses on guardrails and SLO-driven rules. This ticket codifies a compiler that accepts hybrid metric targets and produces cohesive scaling plans with explicit staged safety enforcement, enabling deterministic, auditable scaling behavior across fleets.
acceptance_criteria: DSL spec published and approved by PM and Runtime leads
Compiler module committed and unit-tested (>=90% coverage for policy parsing and validation)

End-to-end integration tests validate: a) threshold and PID policies produce expected scale-up/scale-down sequences in the simulator, b) safety limits cap aggressive scaling, c) cooldowns prevent oscillation
Telemetry: per-policy decision logs emitted (reason, input metric vector, chosen action, pre/post pool state)
Console can create and apply a sample hybrid-target policy to a staging Dedicated pool and perform a canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
Performance: compiler path adds <30ms median latency to request route evaluation in the control plane

comments: 2026-03-03 — Rohan Patel: Initial design doc uploaded. TL;DR: introduce "hybrid_target" array that lets users weight metrics (eg {metric: "tokens/s", weight: 0.7}, {metric: "p99", weight: 0.3}). Compiler normalizes weights and computes composite score for most algorithms.

2026-03-05 — Linh Nguyen: Reviewed. Request to add 'emergency_mode' semantics: if observed error_rate > X% for Y minutes, immediately freeze scaling and trigger circuit-breaker; also need an operator-visible kill-switch.
2026-03-06 — Maya Brooks (SRE): Simulator PR shows PID can overshoot with token-bursts unless we cap max_scale_per_minute; recommend default 2x/min cap and 5-minute cooldown window for scale-downs.

2026-03-08 — Priya Desai (PM): Preference for conservative defaults for enterprise customers. Add 'cost_weight' to the policy so teams can trade throughput for lower cost when needed. Also request audit log entry for every policy change.
2026-03-10 — Code review (ENG): PR #1823 includes compiler scaffolding. Reviewer notes: need clearer separation between policy validation (compile-time) and runtime invariants (enforced on apply).
2026-03-12 — Linh Nguyen: Merged validation layer and basic threshold algorithm. Next: add PID wrapper and staged safety checks. Kick off Console wireframe session next week.
notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) Full MPC predictive model vs light moving-average predictor — chose light predictor for predictability and lower operational cost. 2) Exposing many knobs in Console increases power but harms discoverability — will expose advanced mode for power users.
Interacts with Dedicated runtime routing: policies compiled to per-variant configs; runtime must support per-variant max_replicas and step-limits (follow-up ENG work).
Operator ergonomics: policy diff and dry-run mode required before apply. Include estimated cost delta and expected p99 impact in dry-run.
